title: Trump Is Triggering a Middle East Nuclear Arms Race
gist: Washington has sanctioned a 30-year, tens-of-billions-of-dollars agreement to share U.S. civilian nuclear technology with Saudi Arabia that could permit domestic uranium enrichment on Saudi soil — without the 'gold standard' no-enrichment safeguards imposed on the UAE in 2009 and without Riyadh signing the IAEA Additional Protocol. Bermant argues this hands Israel proliferation risk with no normalization payoff, invites Egypt and Turkey to demand the same rights, and gives a post-war Iran fresh motivation to abandon hedging and race for a weapon.

insights.claim: Washington has sanctioned a 30-year agreement with Saudi Arabia to share U.S. civilian nuclear power technology that could allow the Saudis to establish a domestic uranium enrichment facility on their own soil under U.S. oversight.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: A 30-year sovereign nuclear buildout is a multi-decade contracting pipeline for U.S. reactor, fuel-cycle and engineering suppliers — and a step-change in regional proliferation risk pricing.
insights.locator: Two weeks on, Trump has dropped yet another bombshell

insights.claim: The deal is estimated to be worth tens of billions of dollars and seeks to guarantee U.S. commercial dominance over Saudi Arabia's nuclear infrastructure while shutting out foreign rivals, with the regional arms-race risk apparently a secondary concern.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: The commercial motive dominates the nonproliferation motive, which means the deal is likely to survive security objections — bullish for U.S. nuclear exporters.
insights.quote: That it could simultaneously trigger a regional arms race appears to be of secondary concern to Trump.
insights.locator: The deal is estimated to be worth tens of billions of dollars

insights.claim: Trump has posted that the agreement is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords while insisting the deal will be approved and that there will be 'no enrichment,' without elaborating on what happens if the Saudis decline to normalize with Israel as expected.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: The normalization condition may be a tactical distraction rather than a binding constraint — watch whether approval proceeds absent a Saudi-Israeli accord.
insights.quote: is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords
insights.locator: Perhaps in reaction to mounting backlash

insights.claim: The Saudi nuclear deal was preceded two weeks earlier by Trump suggesting the United States was ready to sell F-35 fighter jets to Turkey, reversing an earlier ban, which Netanyahu warned on CNN could significantly undermine Israel's regional military edge.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Two U.S. capability transfers to regional rivals in two weeks signals a deliberate shift away from guaranteeing Israeli qualitative military edge — a defense-procurement and regional-risk regime change.

themes.theme: Missing safeguards vs the UAE precedent

insights.claim: The proposed U.S.-Saudi nuclear agreement does not include the 'gold standard' safeguards framework that the Obama administration imposed on the United Arab Emirates in its 2009 civil nuclear agreement, which prohibited domestic enrichment and reprocessing of spent fuel.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Dropping the gold standard sets a template every subsequent 123 Agreement counterparty will demand — a systemic weakening of the U.S. nonproliferation export regime.
insights.quote: the proposed U.S.-Saudi nuclear agreement does not include the existing framework of “gold standard” safeguards
insights.locator: In 2009, when the Obama administration reached a landmark civil nuclear agreement

insights.claim: Whereas the UAE signed the IAEA Additional Protocol granting inspectors scope for intrusive snap inspections, Saudi Arabia operates under a very limited safeguards agreement and has refused to sign the Additional Protocol.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Without the Additional Protocol there is no verification mechanism to detect diversion, so U.S. 'oversight' assurances are structurally unenforceable.
insights.locator: Moreover, whereas the UAE signed the International Atomic Energy Agency Additional Protocol

insights.claim: The 48-nation Nuclear Suppliers Group adopted export guidelines in 2011 strongly discouraging the transfer of enrichment and reprocessing technology, guidelines the Saudi arrangement cuts against.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: A U.S. deviation from NSG norms erodes the multilateral supply-side restraint other suppliers relied on — expect Russian and Chinese vendors to cite the precedent.
insights.locator: In 2011, the 48-nation Nuclear Suppliers Group adopted export guidelines

insights.claim: Israel's defense establishment rationalizes the deal on the grounds that U.S. involvement is far preferable to the Russian or Chinese support the Saudis might otherwise seek, which would pose an infinitely greater risk.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: The 'better us than them' argument is the political case that will carry the deal through — and it applies to every future nuclear export decision.
insights.locator: Israel’s defense establishment has also voiced a similar rationalization

insights.claim: Saudi leaders have stated repeatedly that if Iran crosses the nuclear threshold they will move swiftly to acquire a military nuclear capability, and Saudi Arabia possesses the resources, technical know-how and leverage to make good on that threat.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: The declared trigger is Iranian breakout, so Iranian enrichment news becomes a direct forward indicator of Saudi weaponization — a tail risk for regional energy assets.
insights.quote: What makes this agreement particularly alarming is that the Saudis have never hidden their nuclear ambitions.
insights.locator: What makes this agreement particularly alarming

insights.claim: If Riyadh is granted a green light to enrich uranium, states such as Egypt and Turkey will demand the same right, spreading the capability across the region.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Names the next two claimants — watch Egyptian and Turkish enrichment demands as the confirming signal that a regional cascade has begun.
insights.locator: If Riyadh is granted a green light

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia is not currently an adversary of Israel or the United States but no one can say who will be ruling the country in 20 years, a risk illustrated by Israel's former strategic partnership with Iran, where the shah launched a civilian nuclear program with Washington's blessing that is now considered a grave threat.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Regime-durability risk is the core flaw in any 'friendly recipient' nuclear transfer — the mental model for evaluating all long-dated dual-use technology deals.
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia is not currently an adversary of Israel

insights.claim: Former Israeli Foreign Minister Avigdor Lieberman told Kan that every military nuclear program begins as a civilian project — citing Iran's Bushehr reactor as the basis for its weapons-grade enrichment program — and said allowing enrichment on Saudi soil crosses a red line that puts the whole Middle East into an insane nuclear arms race.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: The Bushehr precedent is the empirical basis for treating any civilian enrichment approval as latent weapons capability, regardless of stated oversight.
insights.quote: The agreement to allow enrichment on Saudi soil crosses a red line. It puts the whole Middle East into an insane nuclear arms race.
insights.locator: The hawkish former Israeli Foreign

insights.claim: Trump's deal makes real the very domino effect of Middle East proliferation that Israel long warned an Iranian nuclear capability would trigger — and does so without even the consolation of a Saudi-Israeli normalization agreement that was central to the Biden administration's negotiating framework.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Israel absorbs the proliferation cost with no diplomatic offset, which raises the odds of unilateral Israeli action against regional nuclear infrastructure.
insights.quote: Under Trump’s deal, the Middle East gets the proliferation risks without the diplomatic breakthrough. It is the worst of both worlds for Israel.
insights.locator: When the Biden administration explored a civil nuclear

insights.claim: No Saudi-Israeli normalization deal is on the table because the Israeli government is unwilling to consider even minimal concessions on Palestinian statehood that would give Riyadh the political cover to sign.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Identifies the precise blocker on Abraham Accords expansion — without movement on Palestinian statehood, normalization headlines should be discounted.
insights.locator: Yet in spite of Trump’s new condition about the Abraham Accords

insights.claim: Israeli Economic Minister Nir Barkat projected calm on Army Radio, insisting the Trump administration has no interest in endangering Israel and that if the Saudis wanted a civilian nuclear program Israel could deal with it, but responded sheepishly when asked point-blank whether Israel could live with a nuclear-capable Saudi Arabia.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Cabinet-level evasion signals the Israeli government has no answer and will manage this politically rather than substantively — raising the chance of a later abrupt policy reversal.
insights.locator: Israeli Economic Minister Nir Barkat did his best to project calm

insights.claim: Netanyahu's office rushed to praise Trump's Abraham Accords condition as a historic leap forward for peace in the Middle East, a deflection strategy of promoting the idea that Saudi Arabia is aligned with Israel against Iran.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Israeli government endorsement removes the most likely veto on the deal, making congressional opposition the only remaining obstacle.
insights.quote: a historic leap forward for peace in the Middle East
insights.locator: Regardless of whether Trump’s new condition is genuine

insights.claim: Having burned his bridges with U.S. congressional Democrats, Netanyahu now has zero leverage over Trump, and while lawmakers on Capitol Hill will likely launch a fierce battle against the pact, the dangerous precedent has already been set.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Expect a loud but losing congressional fight — the deal's approval risk sits in Washington's legislature, not Jerusalem.
insights.quote: Meanwhile, having already burned his bridges with U.S. congressional Democrats, Netanyahu now has zero leverage over Trump.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, having already burned his bridges

insights.claim: The collapse of the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement — which IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, now Netanyahu's most viable opponent in opinion polls, viewed as a strategic turning point — dismantled the guardrails constraining Tehran's nuclear ambitions after the U.S. withdrew during Trump's first term.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: An Israeli military establishment view that the deal was stabilizing undercuts the maximalist line — and Eisenkot's poll strength makes it a plausible future Israeli policy position.
insights.locator: Netanyahu famously addressed a joint session of the U.S. Congress in 2015

insights.claim: Israel struck Iran's nuclear facilities in a 12-day war in June 2025 and joined the United States in a broader offensive against Iran earlier in 2026, setting back Iran's program while the longer-term strategic implications grow more worrying the longer the war goes on.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Military setback without political settlement means the risk is deferred, not removed — an ongoing overhang on Gulf energy and shipping risk.
insights.locator: Israel subsequently struck Iran’s nuclear facilities in a 12-day war

insights.claim: The postwar environment gives Tehran far greater incentive to abandon its hedging strategy and accelerate its race to the bomb, has cleared the stage for a more fanatical Iranian leadership determined to prioritize weaponization, and classified military intelligence assessments reveal Iran has regained access to most of its missile sites, launchers and underground facilities.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Iranian missile infrastructure recovery plus a weaponization incentive means the June 2025 strikes bought little durable time — a persistent Middle East escalation premium.
insights.locator: The postwar environment will give Tehran a far greater incentive

insights.claim: Green-lighting Saudi enrichment is likely to strengthen Iran's motivation to obtain a nuclear deterrent, making it contradictory that the United States went to war against Iran to prevent a nuclear weapon and now acts in a way that invites Tehran to weaponize.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: The central causal claim: U.S. commercial nuclear policy is actively working against its own war aims, so expect proliferation risk to rise from both directions simultaneously.
insights.quote: It beggars belief that the United States went to war against Iran to prevent it from acquiring a nuclear weapon yet now acts in a way that is an open invitation for Tehran to weaponize.
insights.locator: Giving Saudi Arabia the green light for enrichment
